statement: This map is an index into the repository, not an authority over it. Future Gate audits must verify each relevant entry against the current source before relying on it -- a stale entry is a documentation bug, not a contract change.

canonicalState.notes: Defines StateModelSchema/StateModel, the canonical overall on-disk state shape and its schema version.

candidateStateValidation.notes: readStateModel() runs assertCompatibleVersion before StateModelSchema.safeParse; writeStateModel() also gates the candidate model version before persistence. Project/store behavior mirrors this in src/state/project-store.ts.

atomicStateWrite.notes: atomicWriteFileSync() is the sole atomic-write primitive; writeStateModel() and safe-writer helpers build on it.

runlogStore.notes: appendRunlogEvent/readRunlogEventIds/inspectRunlogHealth plus all build*Event() builder functions (~40, including M28's buildEvidenceGatePolicyImportedEvent/buildEvidenceGatePolicyActivatedEvent).

canonicalJson.notes: canonicalizeJsonValue/canonicalJsonStringify/computeCanonicalPayloadDigest -- the single canonicalization implementation, introduced in M23 and reused directly by M28.

sha256Digest.notes: sha256Hex() is the sole hashing primitive; computeCanonicalPayloadDigest builds on it.

exitCodeOwner.notes: ExitCode const map and ExitCodeValue type; AiqtError carries an ExitCode, register-commands.ts maps thrown errors to the process exit code.

boundedInput.notes: readBoundedTextFile() plus readStdinText() are the size-bounded input readers used by every file/stdin import command.

jsonOutput.notes: renderJson() plus the CommandResult shape; register-commands.ts is the central --json dispatch point.

previewBehavior.notes: Canonical --preview implementation (M9/M20). This is a repeated per-command pattern (see graph repair's --dry-run/--apply), not a single shared preview module -- new preview-style commands should follow this file's pattern, not assume a shared helper exists.

evidenceSchema.notes: EvidenceRecordSchema and ArtifactReference/ArtifactKind (M22); the sole evidence-taxonomy owner, reused directly by M28's evidenceSelector.artifactKinds.

evidenceTrust.notes: TRUST_LEVEL_ORDER and meetsTrustLevel(), co-located with the evidence schema (M22): unverified < self_reported < repository_local < platform_verified.

packetLifecycle.notes: Creation via buildPacketContext/computePacketAuditMetadata (invoked from next.command.ts); cancellation via next-cancel.command.ts orchestrating buildPacketCancelledEvent and applyWorkUnitCancelTransition.

executionSessions.notes: Execution session schema and protocol constants (M26); service functions getExecutionSessions/findSessionsForWorkUnit/findAnySessionForPacket (M27).

externalExecutionAdapters.notes: Normalizes Claude Code adapter results into the generic execution-result shape (M27); generic external-adapter CLI path lives in execution-external-request.command.ts.

evidenceGatePolicy.notes: Policy/rule schema and bounds (MAX_POLICIES, MAX_RULES_PER_POLICY, etc.), introduced in M28.

evidenceGateSimulation.notes: evaluateRule()/aggregateOverallResult()/simulate() -- the sole pure, read-only simulation entry point, introduced in M28. Never imports runlog-store, atomic-write, or workflow-state-store.

statusCommand.notes: runStatus(); as of M28 optionally includes a read-only evidenceGate summary field.

workflowAssessment.notes: M32 establishes assessWorkflow() and WORKFLOW_RECOMMENDATION_RULES as the authoritative workflow-position, recommendation, integrity, and project-status owner. Legacy helpers remain only as compatibility adapters over assessWorkflow(); persisted nextRecommendedCommand is a recomputed compatibility cache.

reviewCommand.notes: runReviewCommand() and the runReview()/review-rules evaluation it delegates to.

versioningPolicy.notes: package.json's version field is the single canonical version source; runVersionCheck()/version-check-cli.ts implement the policy's automated checks (pnpm version:check).

ciWorkflows.notes: The sole GitHub Actions workflow (name: Validate), matrix build on Node 22 and 24 -- no other workflow files exist.

testRuntimePolicy.notes: Post-M34 (WU34-02/WU34-04): vitest.config.ts still sets pool:'threads' (M21 rationale preserved in its own comment) and no global testTimeout/concurrency override. tests/workload-timeout-policy.ts is now the single shared source for the two class-scoped timeout constants (SPAWNING_SUITE_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS=15000, HEAVY_SPAWNING_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS=25000); 34 test files apply one via vi.setConfig, all other files keep the 5000ms default. package.json#scripts.validate now runs build before test (matching .github/workflows/validate.yml's Build-before-Test order, corrected in WU34-04) so tests/integration/built-binary-smoke.test.ts has a real dist/index.js. docs/archive/legacy-milestones/m34-validation-workload-policy.md (WU34-01/WU34-02/WU34-03 characterization+implementation record) and docs/archive/legacy-milestones/m34-closure-report.md remain the authoritative history; docs/archive/legacy-milestones/m34-ci-reliability-confirmation.md records the post-closure CI evidence. See also testInventoryPolicy (M35) for the workload-classification layer built on top of this.

autonomousRunContract.notes: M36-WU01: contract-only -- lifecycle status enum + transition table, candidate/safety-assessment/budget/execution-policy/result-state/evidence-packet schemas, and 4 pure decision functions (classifyCandidate, checkBudget, classifyCommand/decideCommand). M36-WU02 added autonomous-run-preflight.ts (real, read-only repository inspection -- exactly 4 already-allowlisted git-command-runner.ts functions) and autonomous-candidate-intake-service.ts (candidate normalization + one-issue-per-run intake + dry-run classification report). M36-WU03 added the first real, mutating execution surface: autonomous-worktree-lifecycle.ts (gitWorktreeAdd/gitWorktreeRemove -- the exact 2-function mutating allowlist, built directly on git-command-runner.ts and workspace-path-policy.ts, deliberately NOT on workspace-service.ts's StateModel-coupled prepareIsolatedWorkspace/releaseIsolatedWorkspace -- see docs/milestones/completed/m36/m36-autonomous-run-contract.md Sec 10.1 for why that ownership decision was corrected from WU36-01's original table), autonomous-command-runner.ts (the one real command-execution call site -- structured args only, shell:false, mandatory pre-execution policy+boundary check), autonomous-run-branch-policy.ts (a parallel `autonomous/`-prefixed branch scheme, distinct from workspace-branch-policy.ts's `aiqt/` scheme), autonomous-run-agent-adapter.ts (a data-only AgentAdapter interface -- no implementation in this repository invokes a model), and autonomous-run-execution-service.ts (the orchestration loop tying worktree creation, budget-checked command execution, and unconditional cleanup together; two real bugs found and fixed by this Work Unit's own tests, recorded in Sec 10.4). M36-WU04 added: a new read-only git-command-runner.ts export (gitDiffNumstat, this milestone's only change to that M25 file); autonomous-run-diff-summary.ts (real diff/unexpected-file inspection, including a rename-path-parsing fix -- Sec 11.2); autonomous-run-validation-service.ts (targeted+authoritative validation via the already-reviewed WU36-03 command runner, structurally enforcing 'no pass without validation'); autonomous-run-self-review.ts (a pure, I/O-free findings evaluator); autonomous-run-evidence-binding-service.ts (the one place that ties execution+diff+validation+review into a final AutonomousEvidencePacket and decides resultState/recommendedHumanAction -- required refactoring autonomous-run-execution-service.ts's executeAutonomousRun into a cleanup-free runAutonomousCommandLoop plus the original cleanup-including wrapper, behavior-preserving, Sec 11.1); autonomous-run-command-result.ts (wraps a packet in an M33 CommandResult, not yet wired to any CLI command). autonomous-run-command-policy.ts's GIT_WRITE_PATTERNS was also extended to recognize git mv/git rm as git_operation (Sec 11.7 -- a real classification gap found by WU36-04's own tests). tests/unit/autonomous-run-boundary-scan.test.ts's WU36-01/02/03/04 sections all re-check on every suite run. See docs/milestones/completed/m36/m36-autonomous-run-contract.md Sec 2.3/9/10/11 for the ownership map and Sec 8/9.5/10.7/11.10 for the explicit non-enablement statements (still true after WU36-04: no CLI command exists to invoke any of this; no candidate reaches execution without a test explicitly constructing every input; no merge; no deployment; no coding model). Do not treat this entry as evidence that autonomous execution is enabled for any real target -- it is evidence that the bounded, policy-checked mechanics exist and are tested, with zero invocation path from any CLI surface. M39-HF02 (build spec Sec 9, 'Prompt/autonomous integration') added exactly one advisory reuse of the M39 executionGuidance decision owner: `buildDryRunClassificationReport`'s new `executionGuidance` field (complexity/reasoning-effort/agent-class only, via the same `classifyWorkComplexity`/`recommendAgentClass` exports -- no second decision owner) and its pass-through into `aiqt autonomous classify`'s transient `CommandResult.data` (never persisted to `AutonomousRunRecord`, never influencing `riskClass`/`canProceedWithoutApproval`/`requiresApproval`/`alwaysBlocked`/budgets/policy, all still computed exactly as before from `classifyCandidate` alone). See the `executionGuidance` entry for the owning module.

testInventoryPolicy.notes: M35-WU01: test-inventory-cli.ts is the single, reusable static classifier for every tests/**/*.test.ts file -- workload class, feature domain, criticality, subprocess/filesystem/Git/built-binary usage, and inline-timeout presence -- optionally merged with real per-file runtime from a vitest --reporter=json run via --run-json. Its generated JSON is the machine-readable source docs/milestones/completed/m35/m35-test-suite-inventory.md summarizes; the deletion-evidence contract for any future test removal or merge lives in docs/governance/m35-test-rationalization-policy.md. This entry is inventory/classification only -- it does not own or change vitest.config.ts, tests/workload-timeout-policy.ts, or any test's timeout/concurrency behavior (see testRuntimePolicy for that).

commandResultContract.notes: M33 authoritative CommandResult/Issue/AiqtError/ExitCode shape (result.ts's CommandResult/makeResult/errorToResult match the M33 spec's canonical interface field-for-field; action is WorkflowAction | string as of WU33-03 to allow the parser-error path's action:'cli'). result.ts also exports familyFailureResult() (WU33-02: convergence target for all 29 local failure() helper files under src/cli/commands/, closes the exit-10 status/requiresHumanInput invariant everywhere), missingProjectResult() (WU33-02: shared missing-project result for the review/next/manage/export/status bespoke pre-check pattern), and parserErrorToResult() (WU33-03: converts a commander CommanderError into a canonical CommandResult). renderJson()/renderHuman() are the sole shared renderers (human-output.ts's renderIssue() now includes each issue's id inline, as of WU33-04); emit() in register-commands.ts is the sole shared stream router -- as of WU33-03 it writes --json to stdout unconditionally (M33 Sec 5.5 stream policy) and human-mode output to stdout-on-success/stderr-otherwise as before. register-commands.ts's root .exitOverride()/configureOutput() plus src/index.ts's catch block adapt parser-level errors into that same JSON pipeline when --json was requested (WU33-03), and the 5 --example-supporting commands uniformly reject --example --json with exit 3 (WU33-03). As of WU33-04, human-output.ts also exports renderResultFooter() -- the shared status/warnings/blockers/next-command trailing block all 7 raw-text bypass sites in register-commands.ts now append after their own specialized body, and review.command.ts routes non-blocking findings into the shared warnings channel (using finding.findingKey, not finding.id, as the rendered Issue.id). As of WU33-05: all 29 local failure() helpers carry a @deprecated M33-WU05 JSDoc tag pointing callers at familyFailureResult() directly (not removed -- assessed as disproportionate risk for zero behavioral benefit over the ~230 call sites); a suite-wide regex guard (tests/unit/m33-exit10-and-owner-inventory.test.ts) fails if any command file reintroduces the exact status-derivation ternary familyFailureResult replaced; a cross-command matrix (tests/unit/m33-cli-contract-matrix.test.ts) confirms all 58 actionable commands expose --json. The external-facing machine contract is documented at docs/governance/cli-machine-contract.md (linked from README.md). Still open: Contradiction F (workflow pointers not threaded through the ~230 local failure() call sites) -- documented as a known gap in the contract doc's closing section, not silently unresolved. See docs/archive/legacy-milestones/m33-wu01-command-result-contract.md for the full inventory, characterized contradictions, and target contract, and its Sec 5/6/7/8 addenda for the WU33-02 through WU33-05 changes.

historicalCompatibilityFixtures.notes: cli.test.ts's 'aiqt CLI entrypoint' describe block carries the original per-milestone command-set/exit-code assertions; later milestones (M22+) split their own dedicated historical-compatibility test files rather than extending it.

sandboxBackendContract.notes: M38-WU01: contract-only -- capability enum (SandboxCapabilitySchema) plus MINIMUM_REQUIRED_SANDBOX_CAPABILITIES, filesystem/network/environment/process/resource policy schemas, an evidence schema, and a pure, zero-implementer SandboxBackend interface (sandbox-backend-contract.ts, mirroring autonomousRunContract's AgentAdapter precedent). decideSandboxPlatformSupport (sandbox-platform-decision.ts) chose Linux-only via an OCI-container backend as the initial supported platform, with Windows/macOS explicitly unsupported and fail-closed (see the platform decision doc for the full rationale -- this repository's CI runs exclusively on ubuntu-latest). evaluateSandboxCapabilities/evaluateSandboxNetworkCapability (sandbox-capability-evaluation.ts) return exactly two outcomes -- sufficient, or a SandboxFallbackRecommendation -- with no third 'proceed unsandboxed' branch; sandbox-fallback-policy.ts is the single function that ever produces that recommendation, and it always points at the M37 request/import workflow (aiqt autonomous run), never a bare process launch. The five sandbox-*-policy.ts files are pure structural validators only (no real mount/network/process/resource enforcement exists yet); sandbox-filesystem-policy.ts reuses autonomousRunContract's isAiqtOwnRepository guard unmodified for the self-management check. No CLI command references anything in this entry; no process-spawn/network/container surface exists anywhere in these files, verified by tests/unit/sandbox-wu01-boundary-scan.test.ts (mirroring autonomous-run-boundary-scan.test.ts's M36-WU01 pattern). Do not treat this entry as evidence that live sandboxed execution is enabled for any real target -- it is the platform decision, threat model, and pure data/interface contract a real backend was built against. M38-WU02 added the first real SandboxBackend implementer: DockerSandboxBackend (sandbox-docker-backend.ts), backed by exactly one real execFileSync('docker', ...) call site (sandbox-docker-command-runner.ts's runDockerCommand, mirroring autonomous-command-runner.ts's M36 discipline). checkAvailability/reportCapabilities/create/cleanup/destroy are real, tested Docker operations (real mounts, a real environment allowlist via -e NAME, --network none, --cpus/--memory/--memory-swap/--pids-limit resource flags, --cap-drop ALL/--security-opt no-new-privileges/--user 1000:1000 hardening, a pinned, embedded-Dockerfile-built base image aiqt-sandbox-base:1, never 'latest'). launchProcess/streamEvents/cancel/collectResult/exportEvidence are honest, explicit 'not yet supported' stubs (never a fabricated success) -- WU38-03 implements those for real. This backend permanently never claims network_destination_restriction (plain Docker has no destination-allowlist/egress-proxy mechanism), so network-enabled live execution remains unsupported by design; only network-denied live execution is in scope for this backend, ever. reportCapabilities() also omits process_tree_control (no process launch exists yet) and disk_limit (no portable, real write-byte enforcement for a bind-mounted worktree exists yet) -- evaluateSandboxCapabilities therefore correctly reports this WU38-02-only backend as insufficient for live execution until WU38-03 adds process_tree_control and a real disk-usage check. Tests (tests/integration/sandbox-docker-backend.test.ts) run against a REAL Docker daemon when available and self-skip with a logged reason when not (this repository's own Windows development machine has no Docker; this repository's own CI does) -- the first reviewed exception to the M35-WU01 'zero skipped tests' baseline, recorded in docs/milestones/completed/m35/m35-test-suite-inventory.md's M38-WU02 addendum. M38-WU03 made launchProcess/streamEvents/cancel/collectResult/exportEvidence real: launchProcess runs a real 'docker exec', bounded output, recording a real per-sandbox event log; cancel issues 'docker stop' escalating to 'docker kill', always re-verified via 'docker inspect' (never assumed) -- because every command runs inside the SAME container, this is a genuine, kernel-enforced (PID namespace) guarantee the whole process tree is gone, not per-process tracking logic this backend reimplements. reportCapabilities() now includes process_tree_control and disk_limit (real but DETECTIVE: checkDiskUsageBytes, a real 'docker exec ... du -sb', not part of the SandboxBackend interface -- an orchestrator-only helper). New: sandbox-command-loop.ts's executeSandboxedCommandLoop, the sandboxed equivalent of M36's runAutonomousCommandLoop -- mediates a proposed command list through the SAME M36 decideCommand classifier (reused unmodified) before ever calling launchProcess, enforces command-count/wall-clock/disk-usage budgets with the same inclusive-ceiling discipline, and calls backend.cancel() itself on a cancellation signal. This is the M38 pipeline's 'live agent process' step (build spec Sec 2) reinterpreted per Sec 1.1's own carried-forward invariant ('no live agent process owned by AIQT' must be preserved): it executes an ALREADY-DECIDED command list (from M37's request/import architecture or a future WU38-04 CLI wiring), never a new coding-model invocation -- no code in this Work Unit calls any model or spawns a coding-agent process. create() also now derives --user from the REAL host UID/GID (process.getuid()/getgid()) rather than a hardcoded 1000:1000, so the container can actually write into a bind-mounted worktree owned by whatever user invoked Docker -- a real Docker bind-mount permission requirement found and fixed before this Work Unit's own CI run, not after. Also fixed a real CI-only defect this Work Unit's own push uncovered (not reproducible locally, no Docker on this project's development machine): the first-ever docker build (image not yet cached) exceeded the per-test timeout under CI load -- fixed by warming the image once in beforeAll with a generous hook-only timeout, retagging m38-wu02-sandbox-isolation-backend to the fixed commit. M38-WU04 wired opt-in live execution into the M37 CLI: `aiqt autonomous agent-import --live` (autonomous-agent-import.command.ts), gated at two independent layers -- the operator's own standing AutonomousOperatorConfig.liveExecutionEnabled (default false; new field, autonomous-run-operator.schema.ts) AND the per-invocation --live flag, both required before any sandbox capability check even runs. New: sandbox-run-execution-service.ts's prepareLiveSandbox (real capability preflight via checkAvailability/evaluateSandboxCapabilities, then real worktree creation via the same M36 createAutonomousWorktree, then real backend.create()) and runLiveSandboxedRun (main command loop, then targeted/authoritative validation loops, all via executeSandboxedCommandLoop, then self-review, then unconditional cleanup in a finally block); sandbox-run-self-review.ts's reviewSandboxRun (pure, checks the one cheaply-available real invariant -- zero files changed); sandbox-run-command-result.ts's buildSandboxRunCommandResult (SandboxEvidence -> M33 CommandResult, mirroring buildAutonomousRunCommandResult). Extended AutonomousRunRecordSchema (autonomous-run-record.schema.ts) with sandboxContainerId (the crash-recovery anchor, persisted immediately after real sandbox creation, before any command runs) and sandboxEvidence (the live-mode evidence, distinct from the non-live evidencePacket field -- a run is always exactly one or the other). Crash recovery is real: autonomous-cleanup.command.ts detects a run whose sandboxContainerId is set but whose sandboxEvidence.cleanupStatus is not confirmed 'cleaned', and attempts a real backend.destroy() (a fresh Docker connection, possibly a fresh process) before allowing the record to be deleted -- refusing, and preserving the reference, if the sandbox backend is unavailable at that moment. Network-enabled live execution remains permanently unsupported (unchanged from WU38-02/03); resource dimensions the M36 AutonomousBudgetsSchema never had (CPU/memory/disk/process-count/output-byte) use fixed, documented conservative defaults, not yet operator-configurable (residual scope gap, recorded in the closure report). Tests (tests/integration/sandbox-live-execution.test.ts) are the second reviewed exception to the M35-WU01 'zero skipped tests' baseline, alongside sandbox-docker-backend.test.ts. Three real defects were found and fixed only by this repository's own CI (no Docker on this project's development machine): sandboxed git needed HOME/safe.directory/identity; a linked Git worktree's gitdir pointer needed the source repository's .git directory mounted into the sandbox too (new SandboxFilesystemPolicy.sourceRepositoryMount, nullable, hostPath===sandboxPath enforced -- a deliberate, narrow, documented exception to 'worktree is the only writable mount', scoped to just .git, never the source repo's own working tree); and evidence.filesChanged needed to be captured via a real committed-diff query (new DockerSandboxBackend.getChangedFilesAgainstBaseCommit) BEFORE cleanup() destroys the container, not via exportEvidence's own post-cleanup, uncommitted-only status check. M38-WU05 (build spec: 'Escape Testing, Controlled Pilot, and Closure') added tests/integration/sandbox-escape-testing.test.ts (real Docker daemon required, third reviewed skip exception): parent-repo write (fails -- the parent's own working tree is never mounted), host-home read (fails -- home never mounted), sibling-worktree access (fails -- a second run's worktree is invisible), secret access (no environment variable beyond the fixed HOME appears by default), network access (denied, confirmed no real response reaches a real command), process-limit/CPU/memory quotas (real cgroup values confirmed via docker inspect), disk usage growth (confirmed via checkDiskUsageBytes), orphan process (destroy() confirmed via docker inspect leaves nothing running), nested cancellation (cancel() while a detached background process is genuinely still active). 'Successful repair' and 'crash recovery' (also required scenarios) are not duplicated -- already covered end-to-end by sandbox-live-execution.test.ts. 'Fallback on unsupported hosts' is covered by a real, no-Docker-required test that runs on every host (including this project's own Windows development machine): a fresh backend on a non-Linux platform reports unavailable, and network-enabled live execution is refused by create() regardless of platform or Docker availability.

executionGuidance.notes: M39-WU01: contract-only decision owner -- the shared, provider-neutral ExecutionGuidance model (execution-guidance.schema.ts: WorkComplexity/ReasoningEffort/AgentClass/ContextProfile/ValidationTier/Confidence enums, plus the composite ExecutionGuidance/ContextItem/ContinuationCapsule/ValidationStep interfaces) and its sole pure decision owner (execution-guidance.ts: classifyWorkComplexity/recommendAgentClass/resolveConcreteRecommendation/buildValidationGuidance/buildOutputPolicy/buildSubagentGuidance/composeExecutionGuidance). Complexity classification uses only bounded counts (scope/suggestedFiles/dependencies breadth, acceptance-criteria count) and a fixed, literal risk/architectural keyword scan over existing Work Unit text -- never an LLM call, provider API, or clock/random source; confidence is 'low' whenever signals are absent or conflicting, never silently upgraded. Concrete agent/model labels are resolved only from an operator-supplied, narrow, additive config file (ExecutionGuidanceProfileConfigSchema, loaded by execution-guidance-profile-config-file.ts mirroring autonomousRunContract's M37-WU01 loadOperatorConfigFile pattern exactly: missing file is ok/null, malformed file fails closed) -- deliberately NOT added to AutonomousOperatorConfigSchema, which is a `.strict()` object governing autonomous execution safety/budget policy, not everyday agent-profile labeling. M39-WU02 added the real, pure context-manifest builder (execution-context-manifest.ts: buildContextManifest/deriveContextProfile/isPathWithinApprovedRoots -- prioritized must_read/should_read/reference_only candidates, a provider-neutral token-count heuristic, soft-target demotion that never touches must_read, a recorded (never-silent) MUST_READ_OVERFLOW warning against an optional hard limit, and an absolute-path/`..`-traversal safety filter) and the real, pure continuation-capsule builder (execution-continuation.ts: buildContinuationCapsule -- reuses Checkpoint.summary/filesChanged/validationResult/acceptanceCriteriaResult/issues verbatim, no new checkpoint field, bounded/deterministic truncation, only open issues carried forward). Both are still data-in/data-out: neither reads a file, an environment variable, or a repository directly -- real checkpoint-store/file-listing wiring is left to a later consumer-integration Work Unit. composeExecutionGuidance (execution-guidance.ts) now calls buildContextManifest/buildContinuationCapsule whenever a caller supplies `contextManifestInput`/`continuationInput`; omitting either preserves M39-WU01's exact placeholder/`null` behavior, so no existing caller's output changes. M39-WU03 added the shared rendering layer (execution-guidance-render.ts: renderExecutionGuidanceHuman -- the exact Sec 9 compact block shape, never embedding item paths or reason text; renderExecutionGuidancePromptNote -- a short 'follow the guidance, expand only on evidence' instruction) and a real, callable (but still unwired) project-config resolver (execution-guidance-profile-resolution-service.ts's resolveExecutionGuidanceProfileConfig, mirroring autonomous-shared.ts's M37-WU01 resolveOperatorConfigOrFail convention exactly: default filename `aiqt.execution-guidance.config.json` in `cwd`, explicit-path override, never required to exist -- deliberately no CLI-flag/env-var layer yet since no command consumes one). `ExecutionGuidance` itself round-trips losslessly through JSON (verified by test), so no separate JSON-rendering function was needed. No CLI command, packet builder, preview renderer, prompt driver, or autonomous surface calls any of this yet. M39-WU04 added execution-validation-classifier.ts's classifyValidationCommand/classifyValidationCommands -- a pure, conservative classifier over a Work Unit's own validationCommands strings, recognizing only this repository's own known script shapes (pnpm typecheck/lint/build -> static, bare pnpm test/validate/vitest -> full, a scoped `vitest run <path>` -> focused, explicit impacted/milestone keywords, anything else -> unclassified, never guessed into a lenient tier) -- and wired it into buildValidationGuidance (execution-guidance.ts) via a new optional `explicitValidationCommands` input: real classified commands populate `requiredNow` (an unclassified command is required now, not silently deferred), a full/milestone-tier command found without `explicitFullSuiteReason` stays deferred but is recorded as a visible reason. WU39-04 is also the first Work Unit to wire real CLI integration: next-selection-helpers.ts's new buildExecutionGuidanceForWorkUnit (called identically by next.command.ts and next-preview.command.ts, guaranteeing preview/apply parity) composes real guidance from the selected WorkUnit's own objective/scope/acceptanceCriteria/suggestedFiles/agentContextRefs/dependencies/validationCommands plus resolveExecutionGuidanceProfileConfig, exposed as a new, purely additive `data.executionGuidance` field -- never inside the hashed/persisted packet body, canonical state, or runlog event, so contentHash/state/runlog shape are byte-for-byte unchanged. A malformed profile config file falls back to generic guidance for this advisory field rather than failing the surrounding command. Continuation-capsule/dependency-derived context wiring remains intentionally deferred to WU39-05 ('Complete shared-guidance integration'). Verified against the full next/preview/checkpoint-flow suite plus cli.test.ts's historical-compatibility assertions (162 tests, including 'no new public commands registered' and 'no new runlog event types appear') -- zero regressions. Do not treat this entry as evidence that M39 guidance covers autonomous/prompt surfaces yet -- only `aiqt next`/`aiqt next --preview` are wired as of WU39-04. M39-WU05 completed the deferred integration: buildExecutionGuidanceForWorkUnit (next-selection-helpers.ts) now resolves each dependency EDGE id in `workUnit.dependencies` through `state.workGraph.dependencies` (a real bug caught by this WU's own dogfood tests -- `dependencies` holds edge ids, not prerequisite Work Unit ids directly, mirroring the same resolution `satisfiedBlockingDependencies` already used) to find each direct prerequisite's real Work Unit id, then looks up its latest checkpoint via the already-canonical `latestCheckpointForWorkUnit` (checkpoint-amendment-service.ts, M-prior, no new lookup/store) to feed both the context manifest's should_read tier and the continuation capsule. Added execution-guidance-efficiency-evidence.ts (computeContextFootprintReduction/computeContinuationCompactness -- pure arithmetic only, no fabricated numbers, no billing API) and a new dogfood suite (tests/integration/m39-execution-guidance-dogfood.test.ts) exercising three real, non-AIQT-repository fixture flows: a mechanical/simple-shaped Work Unit, a complex/architectural-shaped one, and a real two-Work-Unit dependency chain with both a Claude-Code-style and a Codex-style configured profile (plain local JSON strings, zero provider calls) -- the dependency flow's own real numbers show a 50% context-footprint reduction (exceeds the build spec's informal 30% target; reported honestly, not tuned to hit it). This dogfood pass also surfaced a real, documented heuristic edge case (not a defect): the risk-keyword scan matches 'authentication' in `outOfScope: ["Do not implement authentication"]` even though the text is a negation, conservatively classifying that Work Unit as more complex than a human would -- accepted as the safe direction per build spec Sec 7, not corrected, since erring toward more caution is explicitly the intended failure mode. Re-verified against the same 162-test next/preview/checkpoint-flow + cli.test.ts suite (170 total with the new tests) -- zero regressions. M39-WU-HF01 (post-integration-review stabilization): the M39 Integrated Review found that renderExecutionGuidanceHuman (built in WU39-03) was never actually printed anywhere -- `aiqt next`'s human (non-`--json`) output only exposed guidance via the JSON `data` field, not the human-readable block the build spec's Sec 9 example illustrates. Fixed narrowly in register-commands.ts's existing `next` raw-text bypass site (the same place that already prints `data.packet` + the shared result footer): the compact guidance block is inserted between the packet and the footer when `data.executionGuidance` is present, using the already-built, already-tested renderer verbatim -- no new rendering logic, no change to the hashed/persisted packet body, no change to `--json`/preview output. Verified via an extension of cli.test.ts's existing 'aiqt next human mode' test plus a full re-run of cli.test.ts/next-packet/next-preview/next.test.ts (77 tests, zero regressions). M39-HF02 (human-authorized post-review closure Work Unit) closed the two remaining Sec-9 integration gaps. Prompt: driver.prompt.template.ts's renderDriverPrompt (the generic, always-rendered operating-instructions prompt -- not WU-specific, so no classification call is made here) gained a static 'Execution guidance discipline' section telling the agent to follow aiqt next's already-rendered guidance block, start from its context, expand only on evidence, and prefer progressive validation over defaulting to the full suite -- zero new decision logic, purely textual policy referencing the existing feature.
